item.title: India counters China's 'map war', assigns official names to 27 Arunachal sites
item.description: India ahs onsistently rejected Beijing's practice of assigning Chinese names to places in Arunachal Pradesh, describing the exercise as "vain and preposterous". India has maintained that such actions do not change the "undeniable" fact that the state "was, is, and will" remain an integral part of the country. Several of the newly marked locations hold strategic importance because of their proximity to the Line of Actual Control (LAC).
item.dc:creator: RAJEEV SINGH

item.title: 'Unnecessary pressure': Ex-cricketer questions Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's vice-captaincy
item.description: Former Gujarat captain Priyank Panchal expressed skepticism regarding Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's recent appointment as vice-captain for the upcoming Duleep Trophy. The young talent, aged just 15, will support Ishan Kishan in this significant role. Sooryavanshi earned recognition after his Player of the Series performance in Zimbabwe, leading selectors to justify their choice as part of a broader development strategy. The tournament kicks off on August 23 in Bengaluru.

item.title: NEET row: CBI claims NTA experts breached 'secrecy pact', face life term, Rs 1cr fine
item.description: The integrity of the NEET-UG 2026 examination was compromised as three NTA subject experts were reportedly involved in leaking confidential question papers. The CBI has taken action by filing a chargesheet against them in a Delhi court. Accused of engaging in criminal conspiracy and cheating under recently established laws, these individuals may face severe repercussions, including substantial fines and potential life imprisonment.
item.dc:creator: KANISHK SHARMA

item.title: Elon Musk's preferred state halts data center approvals; says 'prove' this
item.description: Texas Governor Greg Abbott has ordered a temporary halt to new data center approvals. Regulators must complete a comprehensive audit before projects can move forward. Developers must prove electricity and water use, and tax incentives. Abbott stated Texans must come first in all state decisions. This move addresses growing scrutiny over rapid data center expansion.

item.title: Police put up posters of Lashkar commander across J&K, declare Rs 15L reward
item.description: Authorities are on the hunt for Lashkar commander Mohammad Lateef Bhat throughout Kashmir and Jammu, offering a significant cash reward for information that can lead to his capture. Bhat has been linked to the targeted murders of a police officer and two migrants. In a separate incident, an SUV attempted to run over officers at a Ramban checkpoint, resulting in one arrest after the vehicle was seized.
item.dc:creator: SANJAY KHAJURIA

item.title: Pradeep Rawat's son Vikramaditya recalls actor's battle with blood cancer at prayer meet
item.description: Family, friends and colleagues gathered in Mumbai to remember veteran actor Pradeep Rawat, as his son Vikramaditya Rawat paid an emotional tribute and promised to carry forward his father's legacy. Speaking to ANI during the prayer meet, Pradeep Rawat's son, Vikramaditya Rawat, became emotional while remembering his father, describing him as a man of "honour and respect."
item.dc:creator: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK

item.title: Michael Dell's son Zach Dell wants his Base Power batteries in every American backyard
item.description: Zach Dell's company Base Power is expanding its home battery business across America. The company offers a unique membership model, replacing high upfront costs. Base Power recently secured one billion dollars in new funding, valuing it at thirteen billion. This expansion includes plans for international markets like the United Kingdom and Germany. The firm is also increasing its battery manufacturing capacity to meet growing demand.

item.title: Travis Kelce & Patrick Mahomes’ 1587 lawsuit enters key phase amid court update
item.description: In a legal clash, 1587 Sneakers refutes claims made by Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes about their alleged control of the steakhouse. The sneaker company maintains that the NFL duo has been instrumental in promoting the establishment. This case hinges on the risk of consumer confusion with their branding strategy, as the steakhouse's name incorporates jersey numbers compared to the brand's historical meaning.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Harvard rejected him; he found a grammar error and rejected the rejection
item.description: In 1981, high school student Paul Devlin responded to Harvard University's rejection letter by rejecting its rejection instead. Inspired by a grammatical error in Harvard's letter, his witty reply was published byThe New York Times. More than four decades later, the letter has resurfaced online and continues to entertain readers.
item.dc:creator: TOI Education

item.title: US turns radioactive tank waste into 4.2 metric tons of glass daily
item.description: During the Cold War, the Hanford Site was vital to the U.S. nuclear program, generating plutonium but also creating a daunting legacy of hazardous radioactive waste—millions of gallons of it. Vitrification is at the heart of the solution, as it transforms this hazardous material into glass for safer long-term storage. The Vit Plant has started processing actual nuclear waste and aims for consistent glass production.
item.dc:creator: TOI SCIENCE DESK

item.title: Minnesota solar farms turn into wildflower havens, invites bee and butterflies
item.description: Minnesota solar farms seeded with native plants tripled insect abundance. Native bees increased twentyfold, and more bird species were observed. Taller solar panel arrays allow more native species to grow underneath. Native prairie habitat costs less than gravel over the solar farm's life. Most American solar farms currently lack documented pollinator habitat.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Iltija faces FIR, questioning over 'assault' on cop; Omar calls it 'fixed match'
item.description: Omar Abdullah, J&K chief minister, labeled the Iltija Mufti incident a contrived event, alleging that agencies are working to bolster the PDP's tarnished political standing. Iltija Mufti faced interrogation regarding an alleged attack on a police officer, asserting that she experienced rough treatment by police during a protest. She emphasised that her struggles represent the desires of all Kashmiris, rather than being a personal crusade.
item.dc:creator: NASEER GANAI

item.title: Roman Reigns vs. Brock Lesnar net worth in 2026: WWE salaries, earnings & more
item.description: Roman Reigns and Brock Lesnar have contributed to the modern era of WWE. Mostly, with blockbuster rivalries, championship reigns and record-breaking paydays. Reigns is currently the highest-paid on WWE’s active payroll, but Lesnar has made his fortune through WWE, UFC, and premium appearances. An all-out comparison of their projected net worth, career earnings, endorsements, business ventures, investments and future earning potential for 2026.

item.title: Which tennis queen rules Instagram? Serena, Sabalenka & Osaka lead social race
item.description: Serena Williams leads active female tennis stars with 17.8 million Instagram followers. Aryna Sabalenka follows with 5.5 million, showcasing her off-court appeal. Naomi Osaka has 3.2 million followers, sharing genuine life updates and mental health discussions. Emma Raducanu and Coco Gauff also maintain significant fanbases with diverse content. Iga Swiatek rounds out the list with her authentic approach to social media.

item.title: Ronaldo-Georgina wedding: 7 football stars fans won’t expect, including Messi
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez are set to tie the knot in an extravagant ceremony this weekend in Madeira. They've secured a historic cathedral and a lavish hotel for the occasion. However, several prominent football figures, like Wayne Rooney and Lionel Messi, may find themselves excluded from the guest list. Other notable absentees are Erik ten Hag and Gary Lineker.

item.title: AI creating more jobs in India than cuts: Nomura report
item.description: According to the report by Nomura Holdings Inc, AI-driven recruitment continues to be more than job losses in the country. Given the country's vast workforce, India is experiencing the "largest absolute impact" of AI across layoffs, hiring freezes and recruitment.

item.description: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey signed a new defence pact in Mecca. This agreement commits them to mutual defence against any armed attack. The deal combines Saudi financial power, Turkish defence industry, and Pakistan's military strength. It comes amid regional tensions involving Iran, Israel, and the United States. This pact signals a shift towards regional security architecture development.

With Rodri entering the final year of his contract, uncertainty over his future continues. Barcelona remain interested, while City are already exploring potential replacements if the Spain international departs.

item.title: 'We demand that NTA be dissolved': CJP on CBI charge sheet in NEET 2026 case
item.description: The CBI has filed a chargesheet in the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case. This investigation implicates several NTA-appointed subject experts in a multi-state conspiracy. Leaked questions were allegedly circulated through intermediaries for financial gain. The Cockroach Janta Party demands the NTA's dissolution and conversion into a new commission. They also seek a thorough probe into all recent paper leaks across India.

item.title: Onion, oil or chicken: What made your thali costlier in July
item.description: In July, the prices for home-cooked thalis surged compared to the previous year, with vegetarian options increasing by four percent and non-vegetarian increasing by nine percent. The rise in costs was driven by expensive onions, vegetable oil, and LPG for vegetarian meals, while non-vegetarian thalis were notably affected by higher broiler chicken prices. Nevertheless, the decline in potato and tomato prices somewhat alleviated these overall increases.
item.dc:creator: TOI BUSINESS DESK

item.title: 'He's like me, but better': McCullum's verdict on England's new Test coach Fleming
item.description: Brendon McCullum endorses Joe Root's reinstatement as the England Test captain, emphasizing that Harry Brook's chance to lead will come naturally in time. McCullum mentioned that England remains committed to nurturing Brook's leadership abilities. Additionally, Stephen Fleming has taken over as the head coach for the red-ball team and is regarded as an exceptional choice to follow McCullum's lead.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: Education, jobs, inflation: CJP launches petition asking PM Modi to address India's youth
item.description: The Cockroach Janta Party has initiated an online petition directed at Prime Minister Modi, urging him to tackle pressing youth issues in education and job creation. Highlighting unemployment as a critical national challenge, the party celebrated the recent resignation of the Union Education Minister. With an aim for nationwide growth, the CJP is gearing up for grassroots mobilization to address these concerns.
item.dc:creator: KANISHK SHARMA

item.title: Will you have to pay to use UPI? 7 FAQs on possible MDR & what it means for consumers
item.description: The government is expected to permit a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) of between 0.25% and 0.4% on UPI transactions above Rs 2,000 made to businesses, while person-to-person payments are likely to remain outside the scope of the proposed levy. The proposal is not expected to affect routine purchases such as milk, vegetables, groceries or payments for auto-rickshaw and taxi services.
item.dc:creator: SMRITI JAIN

item.title: 'Avoid Lutyens web': PM Modi's advice to 45 NDA MPs at breakfast meet
item.description: In the meeting, which also included the rebel factions from the Uddhav Sena and Mamata Banerjee's TMC, PM Modi said: "No one should say anything trashy on TV. Maintain full dignity at all times. Engage actively in social media through Facebook, Instagram and X; interact with youth, inform government welfare work, encourage youth for sports activities." Modi advised the MPs to follow the party line and calmly present their views on every issue.
item.dc:creator: RAJEEV SINGH

item.title: 'Get Harshit Rana and Rinku Singh': Ashwin names MI's ideal Hardik Pandya trade
item.description: Speculation surrounds Hardik Pandya's future with the Mumbai Indians franchise. Ravichandran Ashwin discussed potential IPL trade scenarios involving other teams. He suggested Kolkata Knight Riders could be a strong contender for Pandya. Ashwin believes Mumbai must receive significant player value in any deal. The Mumbai Indians are considering rival team strengthening in trade discussions.

item.title: Food for thought: Global food prices rise in July as cereals, sugar turn costly
item.description: In July, global food prices saw a notable rise, with cereals, vegetable oils, and sugar reflecting increased costs. Wheat and maize surged due to weather conditions and market apprehensions. Vegetable oils peaked since June 2022, bolstered by robust demand. Sugar prices also rebounded, driven by weather impacts and expectations around ethanol use. Conversely, meat and dairy prices faced a downturn during this period.

item.description: On the sets of Kaun Banega Crorepati, Amitabh Bachchan shared a heartfelt explanation behind his signature tinted glasses, noting that they adeptly hide the signs of aging around his eyes. His emotional admission was accompanied by an apology for delays attributed to technical adjustments. The legendary actor is currently enjoying the success of his latest project, Kalki 2898 AD. Read on to know more.

item.title: 'US itself regulates foreign funds': MEA hits back at American lawmaker's FCRA Bill remark
item.description: Ministry of external affairs rejected criticism of its foreign funding law. The ministry stated that legislative matters are internal decisions for Parliament. Several countries, including the United States, also regulate foreign financing. A US Congressman criticized proposed amendments to India's Foreign Contribution Regulation Act. He warned these changes could affect India-US bilateral relations.

item.title: Rain fury grips Delhi-NCR: Waterlogging cripples commute amid IMD's red alert
item.description: Delhi and NCR experienced heavy rainfall on Friday morning. Waterlogging affected several areas, including Safdarjung Hospital and the airport. Traffic movement was significantly disrupted across the city and its surroundings. The India Meteorological Department recorded substantial rainfall amounts in various locations. Light rainfall is expected to continue over Delhi for the next two days.

item.title: 'Exercise restraint, act according to law': US urges Pakistan amid PoK crackdown
item.description: The United States has called on Pakistan to show restraint amidst escalating protests and violence. Officials emphasized the importance of creating conditions that foster free and fair elections while ensuring information access. Protests in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir concerning refugee representation have resulted in numerous casualties. Additionally, voting in seven constituencies has been delayed due to security issues, with the government countering casualty estimates as inflated.

item.title: 'Why fear eggs in politics?' SC tells Mauha freedom fighter took bullets to chest
item.description: A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu said it was not inclined to interfere with the high court's direction requiring the Krishnanagar MP to join the investigation. item.title: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan & Turkey sign 'Mecca' pact for mutual defence; India reacts
item.description: The agreement was signed following a joint defence summit attended by Saudi crown prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish president Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Pakistani prime minister Shehbaz Sharif, who attended after performing the Umrah pilgrimage in the city. According to Pakistan's foreign ministry, the pact is "guided by the longstanding historical ties among the three states, based on the enduring bonds of brotherhood.

item.title: Watch: Locals use makeshift raft to ferry schoolkids through flooded Delhi streets
item.description: Heavy rain lashed Delhi, inundating low-lying areas and disrupting traffic significantly. Residents in Valmiki Basti waded through waist-deep water, facing decades of recurring flooding. The Municipal Corporation of Delhi received numerous complaints of tree fall and waterlogging across the city. Traffic slowed on major roads, and waterlogging affected key points like Mahipalpur T-Point. The India Meteorological Department issued a red alert, forecasting more rain.
item.dc:creator: VRITI JAIN
